title: Vrsar with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Costs and Verdict
metaDescription: Vrsar with a dog in 2027: dog beaches, restaurant and ferry rules, €7–15 nightly pet fees, best months, vet basics and EU pet passport rules.
content:
## Dog beaches in Vrsar

Vrsar has about four to five signposted dog beaches, mostly shingle, rock and concrete platforms rather than sand. The tourist board lists dog beaches near Camp Orsera, at the Montraker public beach, at Petalon and at Koversada (the naturist camp). Porto Sole campsite has its own dog beach with four dog showers. Smaller dog spots such as Luka (about 40 m long, natural shade) and Fajban lie within roughly 1.1 km of each other along the coast.

The rule is simple: dogs may swim only where a beach is labelled as a dog beach. Green areas and pine shade next to other beaches are open to dogs on a leash.

### Dogs on other beaches

Ordinary town beaches and Blue Flag beaches in Istria generally do not allow dogs. A beach without a prohibition sign is not an invitation. Complaints from other bathers are common and shade is usually limited. Use the marked sections and avoid the middle of the day.

## Dogs in Vrsar old town and restaurants

The old town sits on a small hill above the harbour and is walkable with a dog on a leash. The streets are cobbled and stone steps hold heat in summer, so check the surface with your hand at midday. Dogs are accepted on most restaurant terraces in Istria, and indoors the decision is up to each venue. Ask before sitting down. Dogs are not allowed in food shops, markets or bakery interiors, so tie-up or hand-over arrangements are needed.

**Opinion:** The harbour promenade from the marina towards the town beach is the best dog walk in Vrsar. It is flat, shaded in parts and has sea access, so there is little reason to drive anywhere else for the evening walk.

## National parks, ferries and catamarans

Vrsar has no national park of its own. The nearby Lim Fjord (Limski kanal) is a protected landscape reachable by road and walking trails. National parks in Croatia, such as Brijuni, usually restrict dogs or require a leash, and rules differ per park, so confirm the current rule before booking a trip. Excursion boats and catamarans set their own policy. Most operators accept dogs on a leash and may refuse them on cruises with food service. Ask when booking and do not assume. Vrsar is not a hub for car ferries, so car-ferry rules matter only if you add an island trip elsewhere.

## What accommodation charges for a dog in Vrsar

Pet fees in Vrsar are typically per animal, per night:

- Maistra Camping Porto Sole mobile homes: €10 per pet per night, limit of one pet; dog beds and bowls are provided in the mobile homes.
- Camping pitches at Porto Sole: from about €7 per dog per night.
- Maistra Select Riva Apartments: €10 per night.
- Porton Nature Hideouts: €15 per pet per night.
- Camping Resort Tina: no extra fee listed.

Private apartments and villas charge between €5 and €15 per night, or a flat cleaning fee. Confirm the exact amount and the size limit in writing before booking. Typical pet-friendly stays cost around €65–125 per night outside peak weeks, rising in July and August.

## Summer heat and best months to visit

July and August bring air temperatures of 30°C or more, and hot pavements and rock beaches become uncomfortable for paws. September is the best month: the sea is still warm, crowds fall and dog restrictions are looser in some places. May and June are the next best. Walk before 9:00 or after 18:00 in summer, carry water, and never leave a dog in a parked car. Porto Sole campsite stays open all year, which suits an off-season trip.

## Vet basics

Porto Sole campsite arranges on-call veterinary service through its reception. For other stays, ask the host for the nearest clinic. Poreč, about 10 km north, has the closest larger practices. Save a vet number before travelling, carry vaccination records, and use tick and sandfly prevention, as both are present in Istria in warm months.

## EU pet passport rules for driving in

A dog entering Croatia needs:

1. An ISO microchip (implanted before the rabies vaccination).
2. A valid rabies vaccination, given at least 21 days before travel.
3. An EU pet passport, or an animal health certificate for dogs from non-EU countries such as the UK.
4. A maximum of five pets per traveller on non-commercial trips.

Croatia is in the EU, so there is no tapeworm treatment requirement for entry. Dogs from outside the EU should enter through a designated border crossing, and the rules for the return journey depend on the home country. Check them before leaving.

## Verdict: how dog-friendly is Vrsar?

Vrsar is highly dog-friendly, around 8.5 out of 10. It has several marked dog beaches, campsites with dog showers and bags, and affordable pet fees. The limits are rocky beaches, summer heat and a restriction on dogs at ordinary town beaches. For a dog holiday, choose a campsite or apartment near a marked beach and come in May, June or September.

faq.question: Are there official dog beaches in Vrsar?
faq.answer: Yes. Vrsar has about four to five, including Montraker public beach, Petalon, Camp Orsera, Porto Sole and Koversada. Dogs can swim only on beaches labelled as dog beaches.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in Vrsar old town and restaurants?
faq.answer: Dogs on a leash can walk through the old town. Most terraces accept dogs, and indoor access is decided by each restaurant, so ask first.

faq.question: How much does a dog cost in Vrsar accommodation?
faq.answer: Fees are typically €7–15 per dog per night. Porto Sole mobile homes charge €10 and pitches from about €7, while Camping Resort Tina lists no fee.

faq.question: What is the best month to visit Vrsar with a dog?
faq.answer: September is best, because of warm sea, fewer people and milder daytime heat. May and June are good alternatives, while July and August are hot for dogs.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia?
faq.answer: A dog needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days earlier and an EU pet passport or health certificate. No tapeworm treatment is required for Croatia.

quickAnswer: Vrsar is very dog-friendly. Several official dog beaches are on the coast: Montraker public beach, Porto Sole, Petalon, Orsera and Koversada. Most campsites and apartments accept dogs, usually for €7–15 per night. Dogs need a microchip, a valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport. September and May are the best months.
